title: Provider-Scoped Model Routing & DB as Single Source

tasks.title: Prisma migration: composite unique, is_default_provider, FK
tasks.description: Modify the model_proxy_models table schema to support multiple providers with the same model name. Drop the global unique on modelName, add composite unique on (model_name, provider_name), add is_default_provider column with partial unique index, and add FK to model_proxy_providers.
acceptanceCriteria: Partial unique index: only one row per model_name can have is_default_provider = true
FK providerName → model_proxy_providers(name) ON DELETE SET NULL exists
Existing data survives migration (no rows lost)
requirements: REQ-1: Schema DB changes for provider-scoped models
REQ-6: Default by model via is_default_provider flag
REQ-5: Edge case — FK ON DELETE SET NULL

steps.title: Update Prisma schema
steps.description: In repositories/model-proxy-repository/prisma/schema.prisma, modify the ModelProxyModel model: (1) Remove @unique from modelName, (2) Add is_default_provider Boolean @default(false) @map('is_default_provider'), (3) Add @@unique([model_name, provider_name]), (4) Add FK relation to ModelProxyProvider on providerName field with onDelete: SetNull. The providerName field already exists — add a relation block for it.
steps.expectedResult: Prisma schema compiles with prisma validate

steps.title: Create migration
steps.description: Run pnpm --filter @lite-llm/model-proxy-repository exec prisma migrate dev --name provider_scoped_models to generate the migration. Then edit the generated migration.sql to add the partial unique index for is_default_provider (Prisma doesn't generate partial indexes natively).
steps.command: pnpm --filter @lite-llm/model-proxy-repository exec prisma migrate dev --name provider_scoped_models
steps.expectedResult: Migration file created at repositories/model-proxy-repository/prisma/migrations/20260701XXXXXX_provider_scoped_models/migration.sql
steps.codeExample:
-- Add to migration.sql after the ALTER TABLE statements:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "model_proxy_models_model_name_default_key"
  ON "model_proxy_models" ("model_name")
  WHERE "is_default_provider" = true;

steps.title: Verify migration applies
steps.description: Run pnpm --filter @lite-llm/model-proxy-repository db:migrate to apply the migration and verify it succeeds against the local database.
steps.expectedResult: Migration applies without errors; existing model rows are preserved

notes: The partial unique index must be added manually to the migration SQL — Prisma does not support WHERE clauses in @@index.

providerName is nullable; PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct in unique constraints, so two rows with providerName=NULL and same modelName would NOT violate the composite unique. Application-layer validation must prevent this (handled in Task-B-0001).
Regenerate Prisma client after migration: pnpm --filter @lite-llm/model-proxy-repository exec prisma generate

steps.title: Add parseProviderModel helper
steps.description: In services/model-proxy-service/src/resolver/upstream-provider.ts, add an exported function parseProviderModel(rawModel: string): { providerPrefix?: string; bareModelName: string }. Split on the FIRST '/'. If the segment before '/' is non-empty, it's the providerPrefix. The segment after '/' is bareModelName. If no '/' or empty prefix, providerPrefix is undefined and bareModelName is the whole string.
steps.expectedResult: Function parses correctly for all cases

steps.title: Update resolveUpstreamTarget signature and logic
steps.description: Modify resolveUpstreamTarget to: (1) Accept the raw model name (may contain '/'). (2) Call parseProviderModel() to extract providerPrefix and bareModelName. (3) If providerPrefix is defined, query model_proxy_models with where: { modelName: bareModelName, providerName: providerPrefix }. If not found, throw 404. (4) If providerPrefix is undefined, query ALL rows where modelName = bareModelName. If 0 rows, fall back to fallbackModels. If 1 row, use it. If >1 rows, find the one with is_default_provider=true. If exactly one, use it. If zero, throw 400 ambiguity error. (5) The rest of the resolution (findUpstreamProvider, credential, baseUrl, apiKey) runs unchanged on the selected row.
steps.expectedResult: Resolver handles all prefix/default cases correctly

steps.title: Update callers of resolveUpstreamTarget
steps.description: In services/model-proxy-service/src/service.ts, update the resolveTarget method to pass the raw model name (no longer pre-looked-up). The row parameter becomes optional — the resolver now does its own lookup. In services/model-proxy-service/src/hebo/build-config.ts, update listProxyModelNames to return all model names (including duplicates across providers) and update the loop to pass model names directly to resolveUpstreamTarget without pre-looking-up rows.
steps.expectedResult: All callers compile and work with new resolver signature

steps.title: Write resolver tests
steps.description: In services/model-proxy-service/src/resolver/upstream-provider.test.ts, add tests for: (1) parseProviderModel with various inputs (bare name, provider/model, a/b/c, empty prefix '/model', trailing slash 'provider/'), (2) resolveUpstreamTarget with bare name + single row, (3) bare name + multiple rows + default flag, (4) bare name + multiple rows + no default → error, (5) provider/model prefix → specific row, (6) unknown provider prefix → error, (7) NULL provider backward compat, (8) disabled model → error. Mock database.modelProxyModel.findMany and findFirst appropriately.
steps.expectedResult: All new tests pass; existing tests still pass

produces: export function parseProviderModel(rawModel: string): { providerPrefix?: string; bareModelName: string }

notes: The row parameter in resolveUpstreamTarget is kept for backward compatibility with the legacy ModelProxyService path, but becomes optional. When not provided, the resolver does its own DB lookup.
The fallbackModels (from models.jsonc / DbModelsRepository) are still used as a last-resort fallback when no DB row exists. This preserves backward compat for models not yet in the DB.
The Hebo gateway build-config.ts needs significant changes — see Task-B-0002 for the catalog registration logic.

tasks.title: Hebo gateway: register provider/model canonical ids for ambiguous models
tasks.description: Update buildHeboGatewayConfig() to handle models that appear under multiple providers. For models with a single row, register under the bare modelName (backward compatible). For models with multiple rows, register each under providerName/modelName as the canonical id, and additionally register the default provider's row under the bare modelName.
acceptanceCriteria: Single-provider models registered under bare modelName (no change in behavior)
Multi-provider models registered under providerName/modelName for each provider
Default provider's model additionally registered under bare modelName
Ambiguous models with no default are logged as warning and excluded from bare-name catalog
Existing Hebo gateway tests still pass (or are updated)
requirements: REQ-8: Hebo gateway catalog with provider/model canonical ids
Edge case 9: ambiguous model with no default → warning, excluded from bare-name catalog

steps.title: Update listProxyModelNames to return all rows
steps.description: Modify listProxyModelNames() in build-config.ts to return ALL enabled model rows (not just distinct modelNames). Change the return type to include providerName. For each row, if providerName is non-null, return 'providerName/modelName'; if null, return 'modelName'. This ensures multi-provider models appear as distinct entries.
steps.expectedResult: Function returns provider/model entries for models with providerName

steps.title: Update catalog build loop for multi-provider models
steps.description: In the main loop of buildHeboGatewayConfig(), after resolving each model, determine the catalog key: (1) Query how many rows exist for the bare modelName. (2) If exactly 1 row, register under bare modelName. (3) If >1 rows, register under providerName/modelName. (4) Additionally, if this row has is_default_provider=true, also register under bare modelName. (5) If >1 rows and no row has is_default_provider=true, log a warning and skip bare-name registration for that modelName.
steps.expectedResult: Catalog entries correctly handle single and multi-provider models

notes: The Hebo gateway build runs at startup — performance is not critical, but avoid N+1 queries. Batch the row-count queries.
The warning for ambiguous models without default should use console.warn and include the model name so operators can fix it.
